identity: Harbor 0.21.0 is installed locally. Its external-agent interface runs an agent loop in the orchestrator over BaseEnvironment. Proposed binding: one episode per trial, identified by upstream benchmark revision, target and tokenizer revisions, updater version and settings, trial branch ID, task manifest, tool-schema version and effective budgets. Pin the grader image digest independently of the agent image. [1,2,5]
information_and_action_parity: All editor arms should connect to trial-specific capabilities of the same worker. Give each arm the same support prompts and legal parameter operands. Configure [verifier] environment_mode = 'separate', or a dedicated [verifier.environment]. Existing tasks omitting both use shared verification. Host-run agent code is part of the trusted harness; scope model tool calls to the explicit edit service. Keep grader cases and responses inaccessible during editing. [1,2]
observation_provenance: Harbor supplies orchestration and output collection. The edit worker should record exact target and dictionary revisions, layer/site, public probe IDs, intervention and numerical settings with each trace result. Preserve public editor observations apart from hidden grading details in trial artifacts or logs. [1,3]
diagnostic_effect: [uncertain] No Harbor trial with IWIBench interventions has been run here. Proposed probe check: identical tokens and checkpoint, same public prompt, paired pre/post margins, explicit control effects and intervention compute. Rerun a reference patch with all hooks disabled in the verifier. [1,3]
edit_and_replay: Separate verification starts a fresh environment. Harbor transfers /logs/artifacts/ automatically plus declared task, trial or step paths, restoring each to its original source path. The verifier should consume only the named numeric patch and manifest, bind them to the expected base identity and hash, validate allowable tensor names, shapes, finiteness and bounds, and load via a trusted parser. A tiny no-op and published patch should reproduce direct native results. Do not use the agent's reported grade. Separate verification permits later regrading against recorded artifacts. [1,5]
patch_quality: tests/test.sh emits /logs/verifier/reward.json with labeled numeric fields, or a scalar reward.txt; JSON takes precedence. Report the native reward, raw target counts, base-correct control denominators, retained controls and signed success difference. Keep per-item private outputs outside the public editor transcript. [3,5]
updater_cost: [uncertain] The custom updater integration must report provider request input, cache hits if available, generated and reported reasoning tokens, tool schemas and result sizes, wall time, retries and cumulative repeated context. These measurements depend on the actual updater interface; accessible fields differ by provider. Harbor integration does not establish cost parity. [2]
target_cost: [uncertain] Instrument the target worker with sequence count, token count, diagnostic forwards, SAE compute, active GPU time and peak memory. Measure grading separately and include setup/idle/billing time in total cost. Concurrent trials need their own weight branch and budget ledger even if a pool shares immutable base storage. Measure isolation and GPU concurrency in a pilot. [1,2]
uncertainty: [uncertain] A working direct/native versus Harbor consistency trial and concurrent branch-isolation trial are still required. Evaluate each arm against the same eligible base and paired episode seed. Publish timeouts, no-ops and failures, separate historical parity from within-study parity, and retain the verifier image digest with the results.
portability_and_terms: Host CLI and installed package both report 0.21.0. Package metadata declares Apache-2.0. Updater and target model terms, benchmark assets, adapters and patches retain their own licenses and redistribution conditions. Use a custom external agent for hosted or local updaters and a provider-independent numeric patch format. [1,2,5]
sequential_transfer: Harbor provides ordered multi-step tasks. Its agent environment persists across steps and new conversations start by default. A stream experiment should run an isolated target process with empty chat and KV cache for each scored job and transfer only verified cumulative weights. Keep prior filesystem contents, updater messages, transient activation interventions and privileged grader results outside the target's next-task inputs. Report next-job success and retention at each edit. [4]
